# Adjudication Task — Chapter 250

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃250화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|마교.
  6|
  7|스스로를 천마신교(天魔神敎)라 칭하는 그들이 없었다면 천하 무림이 하나로 결집하는 일도 없었을 것이다.
  8|
  9|그러나 불과 넉 달 만에 청해와 감숙, 사천이 마교의 수중에 떨어지자 이야기는 달라졌다.
 10|
 11|구파일방과 오대세가를 비롯한 수많은 정파 무림의 영수들이 한자리에 모였고, 장강수로맹과 녹림맹 등 사파와 흑도의 거물들도 힘을 보탰다.
 12|
 13|그리고…… 그 중심에 무신(武神)이 있었다.
 14|
 15|천하제일이라는 수식어를 가진 불세출의 고수. 그 어느 진영에도 속하지 않은 무적자.
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|‘하나의 깃발을 세웁시다. 그것만이 유일한 방법이오.’
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|그렇게 오랜 세월 이합집산을 거듭하던 정파와 흑도, 사파는 한 깃발 아래 뭉쳤다.
 24|
 25|무림맹(武林盟)의 탄생이었다.
 26|
 27|치열했던 십 년간의 대전쟁이 끝나고 얼마 지나지 않아 무신의 실종과 함께 무림맹은 해산되었지만, 옛 영웅들이 머물렀던 터만은 그대로 남아 이어지고 있었다.
 28|
 29|새로운 사람, 새로운 형태로.
 30|
 31|“어후, 미어터지는구먼.”
 32|
 33|중년인은 질린 얼굴로 무림맹 앞에 늘어선 긴 줄을 바라봤다.
 34|
 35|아직 들어가지도 않았는데 이 정도라니. 저 안은 얼마나 혼잡할지 생각만 해도 눈앞이 깜깜해졌다.
 36|
 37|심지어 어제 먹은 술로 인한 숙취가 아직 가시지도 않은 상태다.
 38|
 39|“임자, 그냥 시장이나 한 바퀴 돌고 갑시다. 응?”
 40|
 41|중년인의 간절한 귓속말에 부인이 단호하게 고개를 저었다.
 42|
 43|“안 돼, 애가 얼마나 기대하고 있는데. 본선 첫날부터 사흘 내내 졸라 댔잖아요.”
 44|
 45|“아냐. 괜찮을 거야. 저잣거리나 한 바퀴 돌고 당과 입에 물려 주면 조용해진다니까. 성라대연이고 나발이고, 무림인들 싸우는 게 뭐 그리 대단하다고…… 헉.”
 46|
 47|중년인은 헛숨을 삼켰다. 부인의 품에 업혀 있던 아들이 어느새 잠에서 깨어나 자신을 바라보고 있었기 때문이었다.
 48|
 49|큼지막한 눈동자는 금방이라도 울음을 터트릴 것처럼 촉촉했다.
 50|
 51|“아빠. 우리 성라대연 보러 가는 거 아니야?”
 52|
 53|“아니, 아들. 그게 아니고.”
 54|
 55|“흐윽, 흐그윽.”
 56|
 57|“자, 잠깐만. 얘기를 좀 들어 봐라.”
 58|
 59|“으아아아아아앙!”
 60|
 61|“……내 새끼, 우렁차기도 하지.”
 62|
 63|잠시 후, 울음을 그친 아이의 양손에는 당과와 어른 손바닥만 한 목각 인형이 들려 있었다.
 64|
 65|예상 밖의 지출에 중년인이 투덜거렸다.
 66|
 67|“에이, 날강도 같은 놈들. 뭔 놈의 나무 쪼가리가 저렇게 비싸?”
 68|
 69|하지만 그 역시 어쩔 수 없는 부모. 방긋방긋 웃는 자식의 얼굴을 보니 안 좋았던 마음이 조금 풀렸다.
 70|
 71|“그렇게 좋으냐?”
 72|
 73|“네! 진태경 멋져! 산서잠룡 최고야!”
 74|
 75|“진태경? 산서잠룡? 그 목각 인형 이름이 진태경이냐?”
 76|
 77|“아빠, 진태경 몰라?”
 78|
 79|“아, 알지.”
 80|
 81|“진짜?”
 82|
 83|“그럼, 아빠는 모르는 게 없거든.”
 84|
 85|목각 인형 따위에 부모의 위엄을 잃을 수는 없다.
 86|
 87|간신히 위기를 모면한 중년인이 아이의 시선을 피해 부인에게 슬쩍 물었다.
 88|
 89|“임자. 산서잠룡 진태경이 누구요? 당신도 모르지?”
 90|
 91|“왜 몰라요?”
 92|
 93|부인이 한심하다는 눈빛으로 그를 바라봤다.
 94|
 95|“오늘 그 사람 비무 보러 온 건데.”
 96|
 97|“…….”
 98|
 99|“산서잠룡 진태경. 본선 비무에서 삼 연승 중이라고 우리 혁이가 몇 번을 말했는데…… 아버지라는 사람이 애한테 그렇게 관심이 없어요?”
100|
101|이어지는 잔소리를 들으며 중년인은 생각했다.
102|
103|산서잠룡인지 뭔지, 오늘 콱 져 버렸으면 좋겠다고.
104|
105|
106|
107|* * *
108|
109|
110|
111|쐐애애액!
112|
113|휘둘려지는 검을 차분하게 응시했다. 화살처럼 빠르고, 뱀처럼 영활하다.
114|
115|변화무쌍한 초식 끝에 붉은 검기가 뻗어 나왔다.
116|
117|쉬쉬쉬쉬쉬쉭!
118|
119|나는 신형을 뒤집었다. 반 뼘도 안 되는 거리를 두고 스쳐 지나가는 검기를 뒤로하고 주먹을 뻗었다.
120|
121|푸른 화염이 일렁이는 일권(一拳). 멸염신권의 일 초식이다.
122|
123|콰아앙!
124|
125|강력한 충돌.
126|
127|검기와 권기가 부딪치며 굉음이 울려 퍼졌다. 비무대 위에 쌓인 돌가루가 휘날리며 시야를 가렸다.
128|
129|발을 내디디며 다시, 한 번 더.
130|
131|펑, 콰아아아!
132|
133|주먹 끝에서 터져 나온 충격파에 바람이 갈라졌다. 멸염신권의 화염이 먼지구름을 살라 먹었다.
134|
135|그 끝에 한 사내가 있었다.
136|
137|입가에 흐르는 피와 창백한 안색. 부러진 검을 들고 있는 그가 눈을 부릅뜬다.
138|
139|“어, 어떻게?”
140|
141|“잘.”
142|
143|대답과 동시에 지면을 박찼다.
144|
145|쩌적. 발을 뗀 순간 단단한 청석에 거미줄 같은 실금이 새겨졌다. 거센 바람을 헤치며 그에게 세 번째 주먹을 뻗은 그때였다.
146|
147|“졌다!”
148|
149|비명처럼 토해 낸 외침. 주먹은 사내의 코앞에서 우뚝 멈췄다. 엄청난 힘과 속도가 불러온 풍압(風壓)에 그의 머리카락이 흩날렸다.
150|
151|이마에서 벗겨진 영웅건이 비무대 밖으로 훨훨 날아가 툭 떨어지자.
152|
153|“사, 산서잠룡, 승!”
154|
155|와아아아!
156|
157|심판의 외침과 함께 억눌렸던 함성이 사방에서 터져 나왔다.
158|
159|수백, 수천을 헤아리는 무수한 사람들이 관중석에서 일어나 꽃이며 물건을 내던지고 있었다.
160|
161|“이야아아! 산서잠룡!”
162|
163|“아빠! 나 안 보여! 목말 태워 줘!”
164|
165|“네가 최고다, 인마! 목각 인형도 샀어!”
166|
167|관중석을 채운 것은 무림인뿐만이 아니었다. 하남, 혹은 멀리서 성라대연을 구경하기 위해 온 양민들의 숫자도 상당했다.
168|
169|나는 그중 유난히 야단법석을 부리는 두 부자(父子)에게 손을 흔들어 준 뒤 돌아섰다.
170|
171|띠링.
172|
173|
174|
175|- [흑수표]와의 비무에서 승리하셨습니다!
176|
177|- 압도적인 승리! 비무를 지켜본 모두가 아낌없는 찬사를 보냅니다!
178|
179|- 명성이 500 상승하셨습니다!
180|
181|- 명성이 430 상승하셨습니다!
182|
183|- 명성이…….
184|
185|
186|
187|익숙한 알림을 들으며 비무대를 내려갔다. 동시에 한 사람이 표홀한 신법으로 내 앞에 착지했다.
188|
189|탁!
190|
191|“허어, 옥체에 무슨 먼지가 이렇게. 빈도가 닦아 드리겠습니다.”
192|
193|하, 이 자식 이거 또 왔네.
194|
195|오지 말라고 몇 번을 말해도 들어 처먹지를 않으니 답이 없다. 나는 녀석의 손에 들린 수건을 빼앗으며 말했다.
196|
197|“올 거면 좀 평범하게 와라. 운룡대팔식인지 오태식인지 쓰지 말고.”
198|
199|곤륜운룡 백우가 시무룩한 얼굴로 대답했다.
200|
201|“운룡대팔식입니다. 아무리 그래도 곤륜파의 절기인데, 이름 정도는 기억해 주시지…….”
202|
203|“그래, 그 절기로 수건 배달해 주는 걸 네 사부님이 보시면 얼마나 안타까워하시겠냐. 지금도 상석에서 지켜보고 계실 텐데.”
204|
205|“도우와 친하게 지내라고 하시던데요.”
206|
207|“…….”
208|
209|“듣기로는 화왕 적천강 대협께서 사부님의 목숨을 구해 주신 적이 있다고…….”
210|
211|어쩐지 도착한 다음 날부터 유난히 살갑게 굴더라니. 사부에게 쪼르르 달려가서 일렀다가 역관광을 당한 모양이다.
212|
213|거기에 더해 지난 세 번의 비무. 아니, 지금 것까지 포함한 네 번의 비무를 보면서 똑똑히 느끼기도 했겠지.
214|
215|내 실력이 자신보다 한참 위라는 것을.
216|
217|그리고 그것은 다른 두 얼간이도 마찬가지였다.
218|
219|“본 방의 항룡십팔장은 천하 오대장공이다.”
220|
221|“그래. 그런데 너는 오 성까지밖에 못 익혔고?”
222|
223|“맞다.”
224|
225|“그래서 그거 들고 온 거야?”
226|
227|“그렇다.”
228|
229|진지한 얼굴로 다가온 궁기방의 손에는 세숫물이 담긴 대접이 들려 있었다.
230|
231|“…….”
232|
233|내심 어이가 없었지만 고맙다는 인사와 함께 세수를 하고 백우가 준 수건으로 물기를 닦았다.
234|
235|개방의 후개가 세숫물을 대령하고 십봉룡인 곤륜운룡이 수건을 가져다주다니. 남들 눈에는 이게 무슨 광경인가 싶을 거다.
236|
237|잠깐. 그러고 보니 한 명이 비는데.
238|
239|“갈균이는?”
240|
241|진작 달려와서 제 조상님이신 제갈무후가 어쩌고 했을 놈이 깜깜무소식이다.
242|
243|내 물음에 백우가 대답했다.
244|
245|“제갈 공자는 비무 하러 갔는데요.”
246|
247|“어쩐지 안 보이더라니.”
248|
249|본선 진출자만 무려 오백 명이다. 그렇다 보니 비무도 여러 군데에서 순차적으로 이뤄졌다.
250|
251|사흘째인 오늘, 예정된 비무가 모두 끝나면 남은 자들은 서른 명 안팎일 것이다.
252|
253|‘이거, 생각보다 부상자가 꽤 나오네.’
254|
255|모두가 한 수 재간이 있는 고수들.
256|
257|그렇다 보니 어느 정도의 부상은 피할 수 없었고, 백척간두의 승부 끝에 비무에서 승리하더라도 기권하는 상황도 생겼다.
258|
259|‘내가 특이한 거지.’
260|
261|지금 막 거둔 승리까지 포함한다면 총 네 번을 이겼지만 하나같이 일각을 넘긴 적이 없다.
262|
263|가장 긴 것이 이백여 초를 겨룬 것인데, 그건 상대의 독특한 무공을 경험해 보기 위해서였을 뿐이다.
264|
265|‘성라대연에 참가하길 잘했어.’
266|
267|지켜본 바에 의하면 그들 중 몇몇은 특정 무공에 대한 이해가 나보다 깊었다.
268|
269|다만 여러 측면에서 내가 월등했을 뿐이었고, 지금껏 겪어 보지 못한 생소한 무공들을 대면하며 경험을 얻고 있었다.
270|
271|‘열화동에만 있었다면 이런 경험은 얻지 못했겠지.’
272|
273|시선이 저절로 상석을 향했다. 애써 표정 관리를 하는 적천강과 기뻐서 어쩔 줄 몰라 하는 진위경이 시야에 들어왔다.
274|
275|그리고 그 옆에는…….
276|
277|“저 양반은 오늘도 있네.”
278|
279|“누구요?”
280|
281|“누구?”
282|
283|“천면호리 송호. 하루도 빠짐없이 오잖아.”
284|
285|내 말에 고개를 돌리려던 백우와 궁기방이 멈칫했다.
286|
287|“왜? 대단한 사람이냐?”
288|
289|“송 대협이요?”
290|
291|“천면호리를 말하는 건가?”
292|
293|동시에 되물은 두 녀석이 목소리를 낮췄다.
294|
295|“당연히 대단한 분이시죠. 아니, 무섭다고 해야 하나?”
296|
297|“무림맹 은영각(隱影閣)은 한때 본 방과도 견줄 수 있는, 아니 그 이상의 정보력을 가진 곳이었다.”
298|
299|“은영각?”
300|
301|궁기방이 고개를 끄덕였다.
302|
303|“정마대전 때 실로 어마어마한 활약을 했다고 들었다. 물론 은영각이 있기까지는 은영각주였던 천면호리의 공이 매우 컸지.”
304|
305|현대로 치자면 FBI 국장 정도인가?
306|
307|개방의 후개가 저렇게 말할 정도라면 은영각의 정보력이 대단했던 모양이다.
308|
309|과거형인 것으로 봐서 무림맹 해체 후 자연스럽게 같은 수순을 밟았던 모양이지만.
310|
311|‘은퇴한 정보 단체의 수장이라…….’
312|
313|유심히 쳐다보던 그때, 송호가 자리에서 일어나 어디론가 사라졌다.
314|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

{
"chapter": 1,
"decisions": [
{
"hunk_id": "H001",
"decision": "SOL",
"reason": "brief specific reason"
},
{

},
{

"reason": "brief specific reason"

}

Include exactly one decision for every numbered hunk, in hunk order. `replacement` is required only for `REPAIR`.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

<file name="/Users/james/dev/murim-login-new/reviews/mastering/0250/adjudicator-packet.md">
# Adjudication Task — Chapter 250

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃250화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|마교.
  6|
  7|스스로를 천마신교(天魔神敎)라 칭하는 그들이 없었다면 천하 무림이 하나로 결집하는 일도 없었을 것이다.
  8|
  9|그러나 불과 넉 달 만에 청해와 감숙, 사천이 마교의 수중에 떨어지자 이야기는 달라졌다.
 10|
 11|구파일방과 오대세가를 비롯한 수많은 정파 무림의 영수들이 한자리에 모였고, 장강수로맹과 녹림맹 등 사파와 흑도의 거물들도 힘을 보탰다.
 12|
 13|그리고…… 그 중심에 무신(武神)이 있었다.
 14|
 15|천하제일이라는 수식어를 가진 불세출의 고수. 그 어느 진영에도 속하지 않은 무적자.
 16|
 17|
 18|
 19|‘하나의 깃발을 세웁시다. 그것만이 유일한 방법이오.’
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|그렇게 오랜 세월 이합집산을 거듭하던 정파와 흑도, 사파는 한 깃발 아래 뭉쳤다.
 24|
 25|무림맹(武林盟)의 탄생이었다.
 26|
 27|치열했던 십 년간의 대전쟁이 끝나고 얼마 지나지 않아 무신의 실종과 함께 무림맹은 해산되었지만, 옛 영웅들이 머물렀던 터만은 그대로 남아 이어지고 있었다.
 28|
 29|새로운 사람, 새로운 형태로.
 30|
 31|“어후, 미어터지는구먼.”
 32|
 33|중년인은 질린 얼굴로 무림맹 앞에 늘어선 긴 줄을 바라봤다.
 34|
 35|아직 들어가지도 않았는데 이 정도라니. 저 안은 얼마나 혼잡할지 생각만 해도 눈앞이 깜깜해졌다.
 36|
 37|심지어 어제 먹은 술로 인한 숙취가 아직 가시지도 않은 상태다.
 38|
 39|“임자, 그냥 시장이나 한 바퀴 돌고 갑시다. 응?”
 40|
 41|중년인의 간절한 귓속말에 부인이 단호하게 고개를 저었다.
 42|
 43|“안 돼, 애가 얼마나 기대하고 있는데. 본선 첫날부터 사흘 내내 졸라 댔잖아요.”
 44|
 45|“아냐. 괜찮을 거야. 저잣거리나 한 바퀴 돌고 당과 입에 물려 주면 조용해진다니까. 성라대연이고 나발이고, 무림인들 싸우는 게 뭐 그리 대단하다고…… 헉.”
 46|
 47|중년인은 헛숨을 삼켰다. 부인의 품에 업혀 있던 아들이 어느새 잠에서 깨어나 자신을 바라보고 있었기 때문이었다.
 48|
 49|큼지막한 눈동자는 금방이라도 울음을 터트릴 것처럼 촉촉했다.
 50|
 51|“아빠. 우리 성라대연 보러 가는 거 아니야?”
 52|
 53|“아니, 아들. 그게 아니고.”
 54|
 55|“흐윽, 흐그윽.”
 56|
 57|“자, 잠깐만. 얘기를 좀 들어 봐라.”
 58|
 59|“으아아아아아앙!”
 60|

The whole thing was absurd, but I thanked him, washed my face, and dried it with the towel Baek Woo had brought.

[P110]
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar was bringing me wash water, while the Kunlun Cloud Dragon, one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, delivered my towel. Anyone watching must have wondered what the hell was going on.

[P111]
Wait.

[P112]
Come to think of it, one of them was missing.

[P113]
“Where’s Galgyun?”

[P114]
Normally, he would have rushed over by now and started rambling about his ancestor, Zhuge Wuhou, but he was nowhere to be seen.

[P115]
Baek Woo answered, “Young Master Zhuge went to fight his duel.”

[P116]
“No wonder he’s not here.”

[P117]
There were no fewer than five hundred finalists, so the duels were held in sequence across several different arenas.

[P118]
Today was the third day. Once all the scheduled duels ended, only around thirty competitors would remain.

[P119]
*There have been more injuries than I expected.*

[P120]
Every participant was a master with at least one remarkable skill.

[P121]
Injuries were unavoidable. Some people even won a razor-close duel only to withdraw afterward.

[P122]
*I’m the unusual one.*

[P123]
Counting the victory I had just secured, I had won four duels, and not one had lasted more than fifteen minutes.

[P124]
The longest had gone for a little over two hundred exchanges, and only because I’d wanted to experience my opponent’s unusual martial art.

[P125]
*I’m glad I entered the Star-Array Grand Banquet.*

[P126]
From what I had seen, some of the competitors possessed a deeper understanding of particular martial arts than I did.

[P127]
I was simply far superior in several other respects, and facing unfamiliar martial arts I had never encountered before was giving me valuable experience.

[P128]
*I never would’ve gained this kind of experience if I’d stayed in Fire Gate Cavern.*

[P129]
My gaze naturally drifted toward the VIP seats.

[P130]
Jeok Cheongang was trying his hardest to control his expression, while Jin Wikyung looked so delighted he could barely contain himself.

[P131]
And beside them…

[P132]
“That old man’s here again today.”

[P133]
“Who?”

[P134]
“Who?”

[P135]
“The Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho. He hasn’t missed a single day.”

[P136]
Baek Woo and Gung Gibang started to turn, then froze.

[P137]
“Why? Is he that important?”

[P138]
“Sir Song?”

[P139]
“You mean the Thousand-Faced Fox?”

[P140]
They both asked at once, then lowered their voices.

[P141]
“He is certainly an impressive man. No—perhaps frightening would be more accurate.”

[P142]
“The Murim Alliance’s Hidden Shadow Pavilion once possessed an intelligence network that rivaled the Beggars’ Sect’s. It may even have surpassed ours.”

[P143]
“The Hidden Shadow Pavilion?”

[P144]
Gung Gibang nodded.

[P145]
“I heard it accomplished truly extraordinary feats during the Great Faction War. Of course, the Thousand-Faced Fox, who served as Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, deserves much of the credit for what it became.”

[P146]
*So in modern terms, was he something like the director of the FBI?*

[P147]
If even the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar spoke of it that way, the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s intelligence network must have been extraordinary.

[P148]
Judging from the past tense, it had probably followed the Murim Alliance into dissolution.

[P149]
*The retired head of a defunct intelligence organization…*

[P150]
As I watched him closely, Song Ho rose from his seat and disappeared somewhere.

[P151]
I followed his retreating figure with my eyes until it vanished. Then a roar from the crowd rang in my ears.

[P152]
“Waaaaah!”

[P153]
“The Life-Sustaining Sword won again!”

[P154]
I turned toward the cheers and saw Jongni Chu descending from a dueling platform, his clothes reduced to rags.

[P155]
His entire body glistened with sweat, and he was gasping for breath.

[P156]
The two idiots muttered as they watched him.

[P157]
“Life-Sustaining Sword? Whoever came up with that epithet certainly has a way with names.”

[P158]
“He does keep scraping out victories by a hair. In that sense, the Always-Victorious Sword truly is always victorious.”

[P159]
He had earned the nickname Life-Sustaining Sword because every match looked like a desperate struggle to stay alive.

[P160]
Even I hadn’t expected Jongni Chu to reach four wins, but apparently he was stronger in a real fight than I’d thought.

[P161]
*If he’s made it this far, he must have some skill.*

[P162]
Just how did he fight to earn a name like Life-Sustaining Sword?

[P163]
A quiet laugh escaped me as I watched Jongni Chu frantically gulp down cold water.

[P164]
*Maybe I’ll meet him on the dueling platform later.*

[P165]
I hadn’t had much contact with Jongni Chu since three days ago. We merely acknowledged each other whenever we happened to cross paths.

[P166]
If our next meeting was on the dueling platform, I might end up feeling a little sorry for him.

[P167]
“Anyway, thanks for the towel and the water. You can clean these up while you’re at it.”

[P168]
Baek Woo and Gung Gibang took the towel and basin respectively, then asked, “Where are you going?”

[P169]
“Our sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the greatest martial arts beneath heaven… Where are you going?”

[P170]
“To watch Galgyun’s duel.”

[P171]
I had heard Zhuge Gyun practiced an unusual fan technique using a folding fan. I figured I might as well watch his duel and broaden my knowledge of martial arts.

[P172]
I was about to head toward another dueling platform when I suddenly stopped.

[P173]
“Oh, right. Who did they say his opponent was?”

[P174]
* * *

[P175]
*The Invincible Divine Sword.*

[P176]
Zhuge Gyun gasped for breath.

[P177]
When he had first heard his opponent’s epithet, he had laughed inwardly. It was far too grand a name for some unknown nobody with no reputation.

[P178]
But…

[P179]
*How has someone like this remained unknown until now?*

[P180]
The hand gripping his fan trembled.

[P181]
His legs had already lost half their strength, and merely staying upright was becoming difficult. His eyes ached from straining to follow sword strikes that moved too quickly to see.

[P182]
The internal energy in his dantian had run dry long ago.

[P183]
Zhuge Gyun was one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, yet he had been reduced to this state while the Invincible Divine Sword remained utterly at ease.

[P184]
No—he even seemed excited.

[P185]
“Wow! I’ve never seen anyone use a fan technique before! Do you have another one? Show me another one!”

[P186]
“…”

[P187]
At the innocent voice coming from beneath the low brim of the bamboo hat, Zhuge Gyun threw down his fan.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
